  <div class="paper-meta">

    <span>Attention Architecture</span>

  <h3>FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Lookahead Sparse Attention, which uses a separately trained neural memory indexer to predict future context needs and retain only query-critical KV chunks on GPU. FlashMemory reduces the physical KV cache footprint to 13.5% of full-context attention on average while preserving or slightly improving long-context accuracy.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="gqla-group-query-latent-attention-for-hardware-adaptive-large-language-model-decoding">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>GQLA: Group-Query Latent Attention for Hardware-Adaptive Large Language Model Decoding</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Group-Query Latent Attention, a minimal MLA modification that exposes both MQA-absorb and GQA decoding paths from the same trained weights. The runtime can select the path that matches target hardware without retraining or custom kernels, enabling H100-style compressed decoding, H20-oriented GQA plus MTP, and up to 8-way zero-redundancy tensor parallelism.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15250" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="attention-residuals">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.03</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Attention Residuals</h3>
  <p>This work replaces fixed residual accumulation with attention over previous layer outputs, enabling input-dependent depth-wise aggregation and reducing PreNorm-induced representation dilution. It also introduces Block AttnRes for scalable training with lower memory and communication overhead.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15031" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>

    <span>Attention Architecture</span>

  <h3>Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces multi-query attention, sharing keys and values across attention heads to reduce the memory-bandwidth cost of incremental Transformer decoding. The variant speeds up decoding substantially while incurring only minor quality degradation relative to multi-head attention baselines.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02150" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
